region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Chateau LaFayette Reneau sits on the east shore of Seneca Lake in Hector, where Dick Reno founded the winery in 1985 and set its tasting room in a restored, century-old barn overlooking the lake. The 110-acre estate, on rolling slopes of stony shale, has focused from the start on vinifera grapes such as Riesling and Chardonnay. Gene Pierce, owner of Glenora and Knapp, bought the winery in 2013, and it has collected Governor’s Cup and Jefferson Cup awards over the years.

Chardonnay has a long history here: the winery makes a barrel-fermented Chardonnay as well as its well-known Seyval–Chardonnay blend. This bottling takes the opposite approach, made without oak so that nothing stands between the grape and the glass. Without barrel notes of vanilla or toast, the cool-climate character of Seneca Lake Chardonnay comes forward: crisp orchard fruit and the bright, natural acidity that the Finger Lakes give their white wines.

The winery describes crisp green apple and lemon on the nose and palate, finished just off-dry, with enough ripe stone fruit to balance the acidity. For guests who think of Chardonnay as rich and buttery, it is a useful reminder of how the grape tastes when it is left alone in a cool climate. It is a light, clean style that suits oysters, vegetables from the grill and lighter fish.
